thread:
dave_support: Hey team — customer `acct-438` just escalated: huge p95/p99 latency surge and intermittent 504s starting ~2026-02-28 22:10 UTC. Seen in us-east-1 + eu-west-1. sample request_id=req_0a1b2c. Any infra changes around that time?
maya_eng: thanks, looking. Do we have a timeline of recent infra deploys?
eng_oncall: I see a node patch job rolled a new GPU driver + kernel tweaks at 22:12 UTC yesterday to a subset of hosts (driver 535.27 -> 535.31). :eyes:
dave_support: customer provided a repro curl and average RTTs. they hit the hosted text-gen endpoint with a ~2k token context. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 640ms, p99 ~1.2s -> 3.5s. also occasional 504s.
maya_eng: can you paste the short logs and any node metrics? especially nvme/blk and nvidia-smi during the window.
dave_support: pasted from their capture: ```
[2026-02-28T22:13:05Z] request=req_0a1b2c latency=3500ms status=200 model=vicuna-xl-13b
[2026-02-28T22:13:12Z] request=req_0a1b2d latency=1200ms status=504
```
eng_oncall: infra-monitor-bot shows a coincident host-level IO wait spike on the affected GPU hosts and elevated nvme await. also kernel dmesg shows occasional nvme timeout warnings.
infra-monitor-bot: host-group=gpu-pool-3 hosts=[gpu-13,gpu-14,gpu-15] nvme_avg_await_ms=410 -> baseline 4 ; gpu_utilization normal but latency up.
sandeep_infra: hmm, that driver update also changed NVMe driver scheduling defaults in kernel module, and we switched qdisc from fq to bfq on those hosts in the same maintenance window. possible cross-talk between driver + qdisc causing IO head-of-line.
maya_eng: interesting — model uses large KV-cache churn; if storage latency spikes, checkpoint loads / mmap faults can amplify token latency.
liz_ops: we rolled the change to ~12 hosts in pool-3 at 22:12; rollback scheduled if we confirm. I can drain and shift traffic if eng approves. :thumbsup:
eng_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) reduce concurrency on pool-3 (set max_concurrency=4), 2) enable fallback routing to gpu-pool-1 (stable) for production routes, 3) scale up dedicated capacity for affected tenants as temporary route. I'll trigger routing change now.
dave_support: customer asked for ETA and repro steps they can run — shared `curl` example. updating them.
sandeep_infra: we should collect perf counters before we rollback: please run `iostat -x 1 10` and `nvme list` + `dmesg | tail -n 100` on one affected host. Also capture `perf record -a -g -- sleep 10` if possible.
maya_eng: also capture a small trace from the runtime: enable token-trace for one request (low overhead) and dump KV cache miss rate.
dave_support: pasted iostat snippet from gpu-13: ```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz   await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         0.10   18.40   1024k  18000k    976.5    21.4   410.2   2.1   412.8   0.50  99.2
```
eng_oncall: that's a huge avgqu-sz and await. suggests IO saturation/queueing. Could be firmware bug or a bad interaction with new driver.
sandeep_infra: any recent firmware loads? vendor noted a firmware push to nvme on those hosts earlier in the week, but we didn't apply changes specifically during maintenance window. still, combined timing is suspicious.
maya_eng: quick workaround we can roll now: force KV-cache cold-start to reduce random io (temp), and enable local in-memory cache for hot prefixes. Also change disk scheduler back to 'noop' or 'deadline' on affected hosts and see if await drops.
liz_ops: performing rollback of block-scheduler to deadline on gpu-13..15 now. I'll update after 2 minutes.
eng_oncall: also switching routing for PROD text-gen -> gpu-pool-1 to drain pool-3. doing canary traffic shift 10% -> 90% stable.
liz_ops: scheduler change done on gpu-13..15. nvme_avg_await dropped to ~18ms within 90s. :tada:
maya_eng: perfect. that strongly implicates qdisc/scheduler change interacting with driver/kernel. we'll leave pool-3 traffic at reduced concurrency and continue monitoring for 30m.
sandeep_infra: opening vendor ticket for NVMe driver+kernel interaction and gather logs for triage. cc: firmware team.
dave_support: customer updated: latency improving after we shifted them to stable pool and reduced concurrency; they see p95 back near baseline. sending postmortem note.
eng_oncall: long-term actions: 1) revert the driver+scheduler change from the maintenance, 2) add e2e perf test simulating KV-cache heavy workloads before gadgetizing driver/kernel changes, 3) add routing fallback policy to auto-evacuate hosts on nvme await > 100ms, 4) add alerting for avgqu-sz and nvme timeouts.
maya_eng: also add a quick playbook snippet for support to run the small diag commands and recommended mitigations (scheduler rollback, reduce concurrency, route fallback).
dave_support: thanks — passing to PM for customer comms. closing the urgent escalation. :white_check_mark:
